paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His word, and you can build on it. Luke says he investigated everything from the beginning and wrote an orderly account so Theophilus may know "the certainty of the things you have been taught." (Luke 1:3-4) That's not a guess passed down through a group chat. That's a careful account, and it's why you can open this book and stand on it.

Then look at Zechariah and Elizabeth. Both were "righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord," and still they had no children and were well along in years. (Luke 1:6-7) I think that kind of waiting can feel long. But the angel says, "your prayer has been heard," and Elizabeth says, "The Lord has done this for me." (Luke 1:13, 25) A hard road does not mean God has stopped listening.

Now here's the part that gets me, and I say this as a stamper who once doubted a lot in a dark drawer. Zechariah asked, "How can I be sure of this?" and Gabriel said his words "will be fulfilled at their proper time." (Luke 1:18, 20) God's promises don't need our help to come true, and they don't run late. John would "make ready a people prepared for the Lord," and that's the same reason my ovens stay warm. (Luke 1:17) So keep trusting, baker, because what He says, He does. And this story is only getting started.
